raw_response:
Let me think about this year's plan.

---

Ai, 50 years I've been on this land. Married into my husband's family when I was 20 and never stopped working the fields. My husband passed some years back, so it's me and my daughter-in-law who do most of the work now. My older son is at the factory in town — he sends money but doesn't come home much. My younger son comes back for the busy times, spring planting and autumn harvest. We have seven mouths in the household including the grandchildren.

Eighteen mu is what we farm. About twelve mu is in cotton — that's always been our main crop here on this side of Quzhou. The other six mu we do wheat in winter and maize after, like most people. I know some village folk have switched all to wheat-maize because cotton is too much work, but cotton has been good to us and I know how to grow it. At my age I don't want to learn something new.

**Wheat (6 mu)** — The wheat is already in the ground, planted in October. It's coming up green now. I'll spread some urea when it starts jointing, maybe one bag for the six mu, about 10 kg per mu topdress. At planting I put down two bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu, that's what I always do. I'll water it twice or three times — once at greening up now, once at jointing, and if it's dry at heading, one more time. The well is good but electricity for the pump costs money, so I don't water more than needed. Last year we got about 400 kg per mu. I expect the same.

**Cotton (12 mu)** — This is the big job. I'll plant mid to late April when the soil is warm enough. I use the local variety seed, same kind my neighbor Old Wang uses — costs less than the hybrid packets and I know how it grows. Before planting my younger son will come back and we'll hire the tractor to plow and make ridges, that's about 80 yuan per mu for the tractor. I put down compound fertilizer with the planting, two bags per mu. Then in summer when the buds form I'll topdress urea, about half a bag per mu. Cotton is thirsty — I water maybe twice, once at squaring and once at flowering if it's dry. Pests are the worst part. Aphids in spring, bollworms in summer. I spray when I see them, maybe four, five times in a season. My hands aren't steady enough with the sprayer anymore so my daughter-in-law does it. Last year cotton was about 280 kg lint per mu after ginning. This year hopefully the same.

**Maize (6 mu)** — Right after wheat harvest in June I plant maize, no time to rest. It's very rushed, just a few days between combining the wheat and getting the maize in. I hire the machine planter because we don't have one, costs about 20 yuan per mu. Put one bag of compound at planting, then when the maize is knee-high topdress urea, about half a bag per mu. Usually I water once or twice. Spray herbicide early for weeds. Yield around 450 kg per mu is what we got last year.

I have maybe 8,000 yuan set aside for inputs this year. Fertilizer and pesticide for the cotton is the biggest cost. I keep some cash back in case something goes wrong — a sick grandchild or something. My older son helps if we run short.
